name: Shirley
headline: Shirley Temple mania (1934)
text: Child star Shirley Temple broke out in 1934's Stand Up and Cheer! and Bright Eyes; the name hit #2 by 1935.
image_credit: Fox Film Corp. publicity photo (Bright Eyes, 1934), public domain

name: Linda
headline: Hit song "Linda" (1947)
text: Buddy Clark's "Linda" hit #2 in 1947. Written for a lawyer's toddler, Linda Eastman, later Linda McCartney.
image_credit: Buddy Clark, c.1947, William P. Gottlieb / Library of Congress, public domain

name: Deborah
headline: Deborah Kerr's Hollywood rise
text: Already rising, Deborah (and Debra) boomed as Deborah Kerr and Debra Paget became stars; it was #2 by 1955.
image_credit: Deborah Kerr, Black Narcissus (1947) trailer screenshot, public domain

name: Tammy
headline: Tammy and the Bachelor (1957)
text: Debbie Reynolds' #1 hit "Tammy" from the film: 39 times more Tammys were born in 1958 than in 1956.
image_credit: Debbie Reynolds, 1952 photo by Bob Beerman, public domain

name: Samantha
headline: Bewitched premieres (1964)
text: Elizabeth Montgomery's witch Samantha pulled the name from near-zero (72 girls in 1963) to almost 2,000 by 1965.
image_credit: Elizabeth Montgomery, ABC Television publicity photo (1968), public domain

name: Jennifer
headline: Love Story (1970)
text: Jennifer was already top 3 when Love Story's Jenny (Ali MacGraw) arrived; the film boosted a name already at its peak.
image_credit: Ali MacGraw, National General Pictures publicity photo (1972), public domain

name: Kayla
headline: Days of Our Lives' Kayla (1982)
text: Kayla Brady debuted on Days of Our Lives in Jan 1982 (Catherine Mary Stewart); Kayla jumped 7x that year.
image_credit: Catherine Mary Stewart, photo by Tony Shek (2012), CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Ashley
headline: Y&R's Ashley Abbott (1982)
text: Ashley was already climbing for girls; the 1982 arrival of soap heiress Ashley Abbott is credited with its leap to the top 5.
image_credit: Eileen Davidson, photo by Mingle MediaTV (2014), CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Brittany
headline: Brittany's boom: no clear trigger
text: No solid single cause found. One name blog credits actress Morgan Brittany; most sources cite fashion for -y names.

name: Madison
headline: Splash's mermaid Madison (1984)
text: Daryl Hannah's mermaid picks her name off a Madison Avenue sign; the joke launched a top-3 girls' name.
image_credit: Daryl Hannah, photo by World Travel & Tourism Council (2013), CC BY 2.0

name: Emma
headline: Friends: Rachel has baby Emma (2002)
text: Rachel and Ross named their daughter Emma in May 2002; Emma, already rising, jumped from #13 to #4 that year.
image_credit: Jennifer Aniston, White House photo by Chuck Kennedy (2011), public domain

name: Emily
headline: Emily: a slow, steady climb
text: Emily had no single trigger: it climbed slowly for 15 years as a fresh alternative to Jennifer-era names. No evidence Friends drove it.

name: Isabella
headline: Twilight's Bella Swan (2008)
text: Already top 5 since 2006, Isabella took #1 in 2009 after Twilight's film made Bella (Kristen Stewart) a household name.
image_credit: Kristen Stewart, photo by Nicolas Genin (2009), CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Addison
headline: Grey's Anatomy's Dr. Addison (2005)
text: Kate Walsh's Dr. Addison Montgomery joined Grey's in 2005; Addison, already rising with sound-alike Madison, then took off.
image_credit: Kate Walsh, photo by Kristin Dos Santos (2009), CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Harper
headline: Harper Seven Beckham born (2011)
text: Harper was already climbing as a surname-style name; the Beckhams' July 2011 baby gave it its biggest celebrity boost.
image_credit: David and Victoria Beckham, photo by Mike Fanshawe (2019), CC BY 3.0

name: Katrina
headline: Hurricane Katrina (Aug 2005)
text: After the deadly 2005 hurricane, parents shunned the name: Katrina fell about a third in 2006 and kept sliding.
image_credit: Hurricane Katrina, NASA/GSFC MODIS image by Jeff Schmaltz (2005), public domain

name: Elsa
headline: Disney's Frozen (Nov 2013)
text: Frozen's Queen Elsa doubled the name in 2014, sending it into the top 500 for the first time since 1917.
image_credit: Idina Menzel (voice of Elsa), U.S. Navy photo by Chad J. McNeeley (2008), public domain

name: Khaleesi
headline: Game of Thrones' Khaleesi (2011)
text: A made-up title from Game of Thrones became a real name: zero before 2011, 466 US girls by 2017.
image_credit: Emilia Clarke, photo by Gage Skidmore (2013), CC BY-SA 3.0
